title: Enterprise Onboarding: Comprehensive Support, Escalation, Integration & QBR Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended process for enterprise onboarding, integration validation, escalation handling, and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and SRE partners working with new or expanding enterprise customers.

Scope:
- Applies to all paid enterprise customers (Dedicated or Private tiers).
- Covers pre-sales handoff, technical kickoff, integration checklist, known-issues tracking, escalation flows, health-check cadence, and QBR preparation.
- Does not replace product runbooks or security compliance evidence; links to those pages are provided.

Owner and stakeholders:
- Playbook owner: Customer Success (Aisha Patel)
- Technical lead: Solutions Engineering (Priya Rao)
- Support owner: Support Manager (Daniel Kim)
- SRE contact: Oncall SRE rotation (see related_pages)

Goals / Success metrics:
- Time-to-first-successful-call (hosted API or private deployment): target <= 10 business days after kickoff
- Integration pass rate (automated smoke tests): >= 95% at go-live
- Mean Time To Acknowledgement (MTTA) for Sev-1: <= 15 minutes (24/7)
- Mean Time To Resolve (MTTR) for Sev-1: <= 4 hours (workable; varies by contract)
- CS health score at 30 days: >= 80%

High-level onboarding phases:
1) Pre-kickoff (contract to kickoff)
   - SE and CS confirm contract scope, reserved capacity, and deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).
   - Customer provides: project owners, network contacts (for Private), security contacts, and sample traffic profile (QPS, seq length distribution).
   - Create JIRA onboard epic and invite SRE/Infra if Private.

2) Kickoff (Week 0)
   - Attendees: CS, SE, customer PM, customer dev lead, security rep (if required).
   - Agenda: success criteria, timelines, integration plan, SLA review, data flows, authentication (API key / mTLS / OIDC), and compliance requirements.
   - Deliverable: signed integration plan and schedule.

3) Integration & validation (Week 1-3)
   - SE-led tasks: SDK quickstart, sample prompt tests, streaming validation, function-calling verification, embedding tests if applicable.
   - CS tasks: coordinate billing setup, usage alerts, and SLO expectations with customer.
   - SRE tasks (Dedicated/Private): network validation, KMS integration, audit log configuration, and capacity reservation.
   - Smoke tests (must pass before go-live):
     a) Authenticated generation request with expected response schema
     b) Embedding vector length validation and retrieval
     c) Streaming > interruption recovery test
     d) Canary load test at 10% expected production QPS for 10 minutes

4) Go-live & stabilization (Week 3-6)
   - Gradual traffic ramp per rollout plan (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
   - Enable cost & latency alerts for customer and CS (token-level dashboards).
   - Weekly syncs during the first month, then biweekly.

5) Ongoing operations & QBRs
   - Health checks: weekly automated health report (latency P50/P95, error rate, token cost) delivered to customer and CS.
   - Monthly operational review (if requested).
   - QBR cadence: quarterly for enterprise customers.

Integration checklist (SE / Customer) - required items:
- Authentication: API key validated OR OIDC integration tested OR mTLS configured.
- Model selection: catalog model(s) confirmed and version pinned for release.
- Rate limits: quota and burst policy validated.
- Observability: access to per-route dashboards and traces granted to customer (read-only).
- Billing: billing contact and usage alert thresholds configured.
- Security: KMS/HSM keys rotated and audit logging enabled (Private only).
- Network: firewall rules and IP allowlist configured (Private/Dedicated).
- Compliance: data residency and purge schedule confirmed.

Escalation playbook (severity definitions and steps)
- Severity classification (Support / CS / SRE to triage on first contact):
  - Sev-1: Production outage impacting >50% of traffic or complete inability to serve critical requests.
  - Sev-2: Significant degradation (elevated latency > 3x baseline P95 or sustained 5-10% error rate).
  - Sev-3: Functional issue with workaround; not immediately customer-facing.
  - Sev-4: Minor issue, cosmetic or documentation.

Escalation steps (for Sev-1 or customer-declared outage):
1) Immediate acknowledgement: Support must acknowledge within MTTA target (<=15 minutes).
2) Create incident (JIRA/Status page): tag customer account and add initial triage notes, logs, and request IDs.
3) Pager escalation: page oncall SRE and SE.
4) Engage escalation contacts: CS lead and customer success executive sponsor.
5) Cross-team war room: organize Slack channel + Zoom if needed.
6) Temporary mitigation: apply fallback model, traffic routing, or increase Dedicated capacity as allowed by contract.
7) RCA & customer communication: within 72 hours provide initial RCA and estimated resolution timeline; final RCA within 10 business days (or per contractual SLA).

Contact matrix (examples) - ensure these are maintained in team directory:
- Support Level 1: support@redwood.ai (triage)
- Support Level 2: se-triage@redwood.ai (technical deep-dive)
- SRE Oncall: paged via PagerDuty (see team runbook)
- CS escalation: cs-leads@redwood.ai
- Executive escalation: enterprise-ops@redwood.ai

Known issues & common workarounds (living list)
| ID | Symptom | Root cause (short) | Workaround / Mitigation | Owner |
|----|---------|--------------------|-------------------------|-------|
| KI-23 | Intermittent streaming disconnects | Client TLS renegotiation + long-lived connection | Recommend reconnect logic with exponential backoff; enable keepalive; increase idle timeout | SE / SDK team |
| KI-42 | Higher-than-expected P95 latency for long contexts (>2k tokens) | KV cache warmup & suboptimal kernel selection | Use prefix caching; increase batch size for background tasks; pin a longer-context model variant | Serving Runtime |
| KI-57 | Embedding dimension mismatch in retrieval pipeline | Model vector config mismatch after model upgrade | Re-pin previous model hash or run migration script to reindex; add schema validation check in CI | Customer Success / SE |

Support process & SLAs (summary)
- Channel: enterprise customers should open tickets via dedicated support portal (link in customer welcome). Critical issues may also be raised via phone/PagerDuty.
- Triage: Support assigns severity within 30 minutes, acknowledges MTTA targets above.
- Escalation: follow the escalation steps and use templates for customer communications (see templates folder).
- Post-incident: produce a post-incident summary for Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents that includes timeline, impact, mitigation, and corrective actions.

Health checks & QBR guidance
- Weekly health digest (automated): exported metrics and short commentary from CS lead. Include: token consumption trend, top models used, latency P50/P95, error rate, and cost anomalies.
- Monthly operational summary: incidents, open issues, roadmap items affecting the customer.
- QBR structure (quarterly):
  1) Executive summary (CS lead)
  2) Adoption & usage trends (data team)
  3) Reliability & incidents review (SRE)
  4) Cost and optimization opportunities (Optimize team / CS)
  5) Roadmap & upcoming changes (Product)
  6) Success metrics and action items + owners
- QBR deliverables: slides deck, action tracker (JIRA), and updated runbooks for any new integrations.

Templates and artifacts (links)
- Integration plan template (copy into customer space)
- Smoke test scripts (Git repo link)
- Escalation email and incident timeline templates
- QBR slide deck template and action tracker template

Maintenance and reviews
- This playbook must be reviewed quarterly by CS + SE + SRE.
- Update procedure: file a doc-change PR and collect 2 reviewers from the reviewer list. After approval, update last_updated date and notify the CS-all mailing list.

Appendix: quick commands and checks
- Smoke test (curl example):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-xlarge-v1","input":"Hello"}'

- Canary load check: run the canary script in /ops/canary with --qps <10% expected> for 10m; verify error rate < 1% and P95 within contractual SLOs.

If you find gaps or have customer-specific constraints (regulatory, data residency, or custom model onboarding), escalate to SE and CS lead during pre-kickoff so the integration plan includes those controls.
